subject: Onboarding: Throughput/Latency Gate — validation plan & evidence
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rinehart <alex@strauss.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding: Throughput/Latency Gate — validation plan & evidence

Alex —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our onboarding checklist, we need to run the acceptance tests for the initial production roll so both teams have clear pass/fail criteria. I attached a proposed load test plan (strauss_load_plan.yaml) with the test schedule and traffic profiles. High-level goals we agreed on internally: 

- Target p95 latency <= 120 ms for 512-token sequences during steady-state at 50 rps
- Target p99 latency < 300 ms; p99 regression will block full cutover until mitigation
- Sustained throughput target: equivalent of ~60 requests/sec (batching expected); peak tests to 100 rps for short bursts
- Warmup: 15 minutes of representative traffic to populate KV cache before any SLA measurement

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm test window (2-hour window preferred) — we suggested Wed 11/04 10:00–12:00 PT or Mon 11/09 08:00–10:00 PT
2) Provide the test endpoint and any auth token we should use (we'll use a dedicated client key)
3) Any special traffic shape (long-tail prompts) we should include beyond what's in the plan

We will run three full passes (warmup + three measurement cycles) and share raw CSVs + a summary PDF. If we meet the p95 and throughput targets, we'll mark the performance gate as satisfied and move to final cutover prep; if p99 is outside target we'll recommend a spike-mitigation plan (quantization rollback / routing to higher-tier nodes) before final sign-off.

Attachments: strauss_load_plan.yaml (YAML load profile)

—Sean
Sean Gallagher

> 
> Thanks again for the time last week. Per our onboarding checklist...

Thanks Sean — this looks good. We can do Wed 11/04 10:00–12:00 PT. Attaching our first-run CSV (run_20261108_results.csv) from an internal smoke run — note this was against a staging variant and without KV warmup so numbers are noisy. Couple quick clarifications: 

- Our traffic will include a ~20% long-prompt mix (avg 1,200 tokens) starting at T+30m; plan accounts for that?
- We have a legacy client that uses per-request cold starts; can Redwood confirm the warmup behavior will populate shared KV cache for all clients?

We can provide a short-lived test key (will send via the portal). If you want us to run an initial baseline from our side at 08:00 PT that also works.

Alex Rinehart

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 06:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Throughput/Latency Gate — validation plan & evidence

Looping in implementation notes and runbook so the test is smooth. Sean — I'll own coordination during the Wed window. Short checklist for the infra/ops pair: 

- Dev: confirm the test key and endpoint once Alex posts it; prepare the runner to use the 15-min warmup scenario first
- Marissa: be ready to capture token-level cost breakdown and start tracing if p99 spikes; have the fallback policy (route to larger instance type) ready to enable manually
- I'll join monitoring channel and coordinate an on-call engineer from Strauss if we see error-rate > 0.5%

Quick acceptance rubric (operational):
- Pass = both p95 and throughput targets met across 3 measurement cycles, with error-rate <= 0.2%
- Conditional Pass = p95 met but p99 violation; requires mitigation run and one re-test within 48 hours
- Fail = throughput below 80% of target or error-rate > 0.5%

I'll also upload a short checklist to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/RDW-STR-058-test-plan (link to test plan and runbook).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rinehart <alex@strauss.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Throughput/Latency Gate — validation plan & evidence

Alex / Team —

Thanks for running the windows. We ran the three measurement cycles per the plan and compiled the results into the attached PDF (redwood_latency_report_20261110.pdf). Summary: 

- p95 latency: 98 ms (PASS against <= 120 ms)
- p99 latency: 342 ms (MISS against < 300 ms) — most p99 spikes correlate with the long-prompt burst at T+30m
- Sustained throughput: equivalent 64 rps (PASS)
- Error rate: 0.12% (PASS)

Recommendation: provisional acceptance of the throughput/p95 gate. For p99 we recommend one of the following mitigations before full cutover:
1) Short-term: route long-prompt traffic to a higher-SKU node pool for peak windows (we can automate)
2) Mid-term: enable a different quantization profile for the long-prompt path and re-run the spike test

Marissa will own a follow-up spike run targeting just the long-prompt mix on Thu 11/12 09:00–10:00 PT. If that passes p99 < 300 ms, we'll mark the performance gate fully satisfied and proceed with the expanded production rollout. We'll drop the raw CSV and dashboard links into the drive folder after this note.

Attachments: redwood_latency_report_20261110.pdf

—Sean
